messages:
Maya L: Quick heads-up — after last night's allocator tweak the paged-attn path is showing p99 tail spikes on long-seq workloads (not steady load). Repro on GPU-3 in staging.
Ian K: Seen it too. p50 unchanged, p95 up ~20ms, p99 up ~120ms. Looks like workspace eviction + kernel fallback happening more often.
Sasha P: Do we have a flamegraph or timeline from the run that hit the regression?
Maya L: Uploaded short trace to staging:/artifacts/pagedattn-reg-1945. Key lines: increased memcpy activity and repeated kernel selection fallback to the slow matmul kernel.
Cheng W: My quick profile shows KV cache churn — many small allocations + free cycles during decode. Seems workspace sizing too conservative now.
Ian K: Repro command I used: ```./run_decode --model paged-attn-v2 --seq 4096 --batch 4 --profile nvprof --device gpu-3``` Output snippet: ```KernelFallback: matmul_slow  x153  total_ms=312.4 memcpy=78.1 alloc_wait=23.6```
Sasha P: That alloc_wait number smells like allocator contention. Which allocator flags changed in the PR?
Maya L: PR #5123 reduced default workspace_target from 0.75 -> 0.6 to free headroom for multi-tenant. But that reduces reserved workspace per stream; when KV cache fragments we create lots of small blocks and trigger reuse/compaction more.
Ian K: So on long-seq runs we end up evicting and compacting frequently, causing transient OOM/backoff that triggers fallback kernels. That explains p99 spikes.
Cheng W: I patched a local build to bump workspace_target back to 0.72 and disabled eager_compact; quick run shows p99 down by ~90ms. Can push an experiment config to staging.
Maya L: Can we test two knobs: 1) workspace_target=0.72, 2) block_reuse_policy=coarse (prefer reuse larger blocks). If both help we can tune defaults rather than revert the whole PR.
perf-bot: Deploy scheduled to staging: pagedattn-experiment-1945 (workspace_target=0.72, block_reuse_policy=coarse) — starting canary. :robot_face:
Sasha P: Also suggest we add one more metric to console: "kernel_fallback_count" per model route and a histogram of allocation sizes — would help correlate.
Ian K: Agree. For immediate mitigation, a short-term change: increase workspace_min to avoid tiny allocations under heavy KV churn. I'll open a patch.
Maya L: Notes from quick grep of eviction logs: ```evict: tried 12 blocks, reclaimed 2, compaction_ms=42``` That compaction_ms lines match the wall clock spikes.
Cheng W: On the compaction algorithm: we could make it cost-aware — skip compaction if estimated compaction_cost > latency_budget. Right now compaction is aggressive for freeing any hole.
Sasha P: Good idea. Heuristic: compute estimate = num_moves * average_move_cost; compare to p95_target for current route. If > threshold, delay compaction and mark hole as cold.
Ian K: Implementation risk is moderate but I can prototype a conservative heuristic in a few hours. Will test on staging canary.
Maya L: For rollouts, plan: 1) apply workspace_target=0.72 + block_reuse_policy=coarse in staging canary (running), 2) add kernel_fallback_count telemetry, 3) land compaction-cost heuristic in next patch if canary looks good.
Cheng W: One more observation: batching distribution shifted — more small batches (1-2) due to client-side retry patterns after backoff. That increases allocation churn. We should also validate batching heuristics and maybe increase batching window when paged-attn models are active.
Sasha P: Agreed. I'll add a quick experiment to raise max_batch_delay to 20ms for paged-attn routes.
Maya L: Thanks. If anyone sees the canary numbers diverge (p99 up) @channel please ping. I'll keep collecting traces.
Ian K: Will follow up with a short PR for workspace_min bump and metrics.
perf-bot: Canary completed: kernel_fallback_count down 68%, p99 improved ~85ms on canary nodes.
Maya L: Great — looks promising. We'll keep tuned defaults and schedule compaction-heuristic work for next sprint.
Sasha P: Filing a postmortem-style note in #postmortems with links to traces and the mitigation choices.
Maya L: Thanks team — closing the loop once compaction heuristic lands.
